item.title: Ep. 166 - What is Business Ownership? [Business 300]
item.description:
There are fundamentally 3 things that set the owner apart: Risk, Responsibility, and Reward. 

The owner takes a risk to initiate and operate the business, takes responsibility for everything in the business, and is rewarded in return for his risk and responsibility.

Risk, Responsibility, and Reward are what distinguishes the business owner from other stakeholders. Risk, Responsibility, and Reward is Business Ownership.
item.author: Philip Kulishov
item.itunes:author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 165 - When Finance Doesn't Serve the Customer [Business 300]
item.description:
When the Finance function's job of keeping score turns inward, it forgets about customer value, causing the entire business to neglect it. But, in remembering that it's purpose is to give the business incite into value-delivery, the Finance department aligns the business effort for the customer.

Many business problems arise when finance doesn't serve the customer.
item.author: Philip Kulishov
item.itunes:author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 164 - When Administration Doesn't Serve the Customer [Business 300]
item.description:
If the purpose of a business - of any business - is to deliver value to a customer, each function revolves around that purpose. Strategy is to create the value, Sales is to promote it, Operations is to deliver it. And Administration is to manage it.

Administration should be serving to help the overall customer experience, not bog it down. Order and control are good, and very much needed, as long as they serve the greater purpose of delivering value to the customer. But order and control exasperate everybody when Administration doesn't serve the customer.
item.author: Philip Kulishov
item.itunes:author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 163 - When Operations Doesn't Serve the Customer [Business 300]
item.description: In delivering value, Operations must hold the customer as the definer of what is right - right quantity, right quality, right timing - and then structure the systems accordingly. The customer, the business, and the operations function itself loses when Operations doesn't serve the customer.
item.author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 162 - When Sales Doesn't Serve the Customer [Business 300]
item.description:
In episode 161, I talked about what a self-serving strategy looks like. This time we're going to talk about sales. What does self-serving sales look like? 

When the customer believes that your value-offering is relevant and reliable, revenue growth follows. But when you chase revenue-growth, you win neither the customer nor the sale.
